notes: Inputs: a straight-on product artwork of a flat multi-colour figure (character plate in a base) and 1-2 phone photos of the real 3D print. Ground truth for the Helmet Guy example: figure height 99.9 mm, base 70 x 20.3 mm, 12 parts, arms = one oval ring, jacket + pants = one suit.

evals.name: understand-before-tracing
evals.prompt: I want to reverse engineer this toy. Here is the product image (perfectly straight) and two photos of the printed one. Make me a front view I can use to rebuild it.
evals.expected_output: Starts with a written part spec (parts incl. accessories, colours, stacking order read from seams on the print, sources/authority, open questions such as one real dimension) and asks/confirms before fitting; does not immediately trace pixels.
assertions: asks for or states a scale reference
uses the print photo for construction/stacking

evals.name: keep-detail-remove-only-raster-defects
evals.prompt: The shape detail, pose and face are important - don't remove them. Only ignore the defects that come from the raster image.
evals.expected_output: Uses colour unmixing (not HSV thresholds), measures the effective pixel and noise, derives a tolerance (~1/4 effective px), keeps small real features (notch between fists, thumb corners), reports max shift in mm per part.

evals.name: edge-level-edit-scope
evals.prompt: The line at the chin needs to be higher to match the image.
evals.expected_output: Measures the face/jacket edge excluding same-coloured shirt pixels, fits the chin, changes only the chin; the forehead/other parts are bit-identical to the previous version.

evals.name: ambiguous-structure
evals.prompt: The arms are made from two ovals.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the ambiguity (one ring = outer oval minus inner oval, vs two mirrored loops) and asks or shows both before rebuilding.
